overview.title: Exoplanets: Worlds Beyond Our Solar System
overview.description: Thousands of planets orbiting distant stars, including potentially habitable worlds

hotJupiters.name: Hot Jupiters
hotJupiters.description: Gas giants orbiting very close to their stars
hotJupiters.characteristics: Scorching temperatures, fast orbits, tidally locked

superEarths.name: Super-Earths
superEarths.description: Rocky planets larger than Earth but smaller than Neptune

oceanWorlds.name: Ocean Worlds
oceanWorlds.description: Planets potentially covered entirely in liquid water

lavaPlanets.name: Lava Planets
lavaPlanets.description: Rocky worlds so hot their surfaces are molten
lavaPlanets.characteristics: Extreme temperatures, one side always facing star

potentiallyHabitable.name: Proxima Centauri b
potentiallyHabitable.habitability: In habitable zone, but stellar flares may be problematic

potentiallyHabitable.name: TRAPPIST-1e
potentiallyHabitable.significance: Part of 7-planet system, 3 in habitable zone

potentiallyHabitable.name: Kepler-442b
potentiallyHabitable.habitability: 61% chance of being in habitable zone

potentiallyHabitable.name: Kepler-452b
potentiallyHabitable.significance: Orbits Sun-like star in habitable zone

potentiallyHabitable.name: LHS 1140 b
potentiallyHabitable.habitability: One of the best candidates for atmospheric studies
potentiallyHabitable.significance: Transits a quiet red dwarf, ideal for observation
potentiallyHabitable.waterPossibility: Very High - may be ocean world
potentiallyHabitable.atmospherePossibility: Top target for JWST atmospheric studies

potentiallyHabitable.name: TOI-700 d
potentiallyHabitable.significance: TESS mission's first Earth-sized planet in habitable zone

potentiallyHabitable.name: K2-18 b
potentiallyHabitable.significance: First exoplanet with water vapor in habitable zone

potentiallyHabitable.name: Kepler-186f
potentiallyHabitable.habitability: First Earth-sized planet in habitable zone
potentiallyHabitable.significance: Historic first Earth-sized habitable zone planet
potentiallyHabitable.atmospherePossibility: Unknown - too distant for current spectroscopy

exoticWorlds.name: HD 189733 b
exoticWorlds.description: Deep blue color due to silicate particles in atmosphere that scatter blue light. Winds exceed 2 km/s.

exoticWorlds.name: PSR B1620-26 b
exoticWorlds.description: Oldest known planet, formed when universe was only 1 billion years old. Orbits a binary star system in globular cluster M4.

exoticWorlds.name: TrES-2b
exoticWorlds.description: Reflects less than 1% of light that hits it - darker than coal. Hot Jupiter with temperature of 980°C.

exoticWorlds.name: HD 106906 b
exoticWorlds.description: Orbits 650 AU from its star on a highly inclined, eccentric orbit. May help explain Planet Nine theories.

exoticWorlds.name: Kepler-16b
exoticWorlds.description: Orbits two stars, like Star Wars' Tatooine. Saturn-sized gas giant in a circumbinary orbit.

exoticWorlds.name: KELT-9b
exoticWorlds.description: Day side temperature exceeds 4,000°C - hotter than some stars. Molecules break apart into atoms.

exoticWorlds.name: GJ 504 b
exoticWorlds.description: Glows magenta due to infrared heat from its formation. 4x Jupiter's mass, only 160 million years old.

exoticWorlds.name: HAT-P-7b
exoticWorlds.description: Atmospheric conditions allow corundum (rubies/sapphires) to condense and fall as 'rain'.

discoveryMilestones.details: PSR B1257+12 - planets around a pulsar
51 Pegasi b discovered, launching exoplanet revolution

discoveryMilestones.event: First Earth-sized planet in habitable zone

discoveryMilestones.details: K2-18 b shows water vapor in atmosphere
New discoveries accelerating with improved technology

transit.name: Transit Method
transit.description: Detects dip in star's brightness when planet passes in front
transit.advantages: Can determine planet size and orbital period

radialVelocity.name: Radial Velocity (Doppler)
radialVelocity.description: Detects star's wobble caused by planet's gravity

directImaging.name: Direct Imaging
directImaging.advantages: Can study planet's atmosphere and orbit
directImaging.limitations: Only works for large planets far from bright stars

microlensing.name: Gravitational Microlensing
microlensing.description: Planet's gravity bends light from background star
microlensing.advantages: Can detect distant planets and free-floating planets

futureSearches.jwst: Studying exoplanet atmospheres in unprecedented detail
futureSearches.romanTelescope: Will discover thousands more exoplanets via microlensing (launch 2027)
futureSearches.ariel: ESA mission to study exoplanet atmospheres (launch 2029)
futureSearches.plato: Will search for Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars (launch 2026)
